craft_claim: Irreverent comedy builds a solemn or pompous expectation and then lets it collapse into nothing; the collapse itself — not a counter-argument — produces the laugh.

supporting_evidence.location: Critique of Judgment §54 (Gutenberg #48433; English renderings vary, no wording reproduced)
supporting_evidence.note: Kant locates laughter in the sudden collapse of an expectation built up about an object into nothing — the escalated promise dissolves rather than being answered.
The collapse is the violation; it stays funny only while appraised benign — solemnity deflated inside a sanctioned frame.

supporting_evidence.location: Verified via SFE 'Adams, Douglas' entry fetched 2026-09-24
supporting_evidence.note: Cosmic and scientific pomposity (planetary engineering, bureaucratic procedure) is repeatedly built up and deflated by mundane register — secondary-confirmed exemplar of expectation-collapse.

counterevidence.note: Kant's account is philosophical and pre-experimental, and translator renderings of §54 differ — it is a Tier 1 primary statement of the mechanism, not empirical confirmation of it.

scope: Any passage that deliberately escalates solemn diction, ceremonial buildup, or self-important framing before dropping it; narration and dialogue alike.
exceptions: The mechanism explains the laugh, not the aim: where the collapse is aimed at a group rather than a register, clm-tone-irreverent-prejudiced-norm-backfire governs.
If the buildup is not felt (no real solemnity crossed), the collapse produces nothing — ties to clm-tone-irreverent-taboo-register-breach.
